subject: Compute floorplan options and min-GPU ladder for Trident Therapeutics
messages:
From: Cory Blake <cory.blake@tridentthera.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@tridentthera.com
Date: Tue, 08 Sep 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated cluster sizing — initial forecast and asks

Jonas,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. We're finalizing requirements for a dedicated inference deployment to support our generative chemistry assistant. High level:

- Expected steady-state throughput: ~2M tokens/day in month 3 of production.
- Peak concurrency: 45 concurrent sessions (95th percentile).
- Latency target: 200–300ms p50 for chat completions.
- Primary model family: 30B dense and 70B quantized for heavy-rerank steps.
- Go-live target: mid-Nov (6–10 week runway).

We need an options matrix that covers: minimum guaranteed GPUs for the contract, typical active cluster size, burst/buffer strategy, and a suggested ramp schedule tied to milestones. Also include warm-up costs and an estimate of monthly committed spend.

I've attached a usage forecast and a quick note from our infra team about peak windows. Can you send recommended architectures and a couple of price/commitment bands — we want something that lets us start lean but with a clear growth path.

If possible, include a shallower ramp option that keeps the initial commitment low and a heavier option that gives us headroom for a faster adoption scenario.

Thanks — Cory
Cory Blake
Head of AI Platforms
Trident Therapeutics

---
Attachment: trident-usage-forecast.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: jonas_weber@redwood.com <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Cory Blake <cory.blake@tridentthera.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 08 Sep 2026 12:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated cluster sizing — initial forecast and asks

Cory — really appreciate the clear forecast and the file. Based on what you sent, attached is a concise compute floorplan with three candidate strategies. High level summary below; full pricing and assumptions are in the attached PDF.

Quick summary (assumptions: A100/80GB-equivalent vram, Q4 model quantization for 70B path, steady-state token mix per your spreadsheet):

Option A — Lean Canary
- Minimum contract: 16 GPUs reserved (min-gpus)
- Typical active pool: 24 GPUs (autoscale to 40 burst)
- Ramp: 16 -> 24 by week 4 -> 32 by week 10 if adoption meets forecast
- Use-case: conservative start, tight budget, warm-up credits included
- Estimated committed monthly spend: $X,XXX — see PDF for breakdown

Option B — Balanced Growth (recommended)
- Minimum contract: 48 GPUs reserved
- Typical active pool: 64 GPUs (burst to 96)
- Ramp: 24 -> 48 at M1 onboarding -> 64 by week 8 -> optional 96 if demand spikes
- Features: KV cache pre-warming, prioritized slot routing, canary rollout lanes
- Estimated committed monthly spend: $XX,XXX

Option C — Headroom / Enterprise
- Minimum contract: 96 GPUs reserved (includes hot-standby 8 GPUs)
- Typical active pool: 112 GPUs (hot spare + burst to 160 across regions)
- Ramp: 48 -> 96 across 8 weeks; immediate higher throughput for early adopters
- Features: multi-region standby, SLA 99.9% with credits, extended observability retention
- Estimated committed monthly spend: $XXX,XXX

Operational notes:
- Canary plan: we'll run a phased canary on Option B with a 10% traffic slice for 14 days before full cutover.
- Fallbacks: automatic downgrade to a compatible quantized model if burst capacity exhausted.
- Warm-start: prefix caching and model warmers to reduce cold first-token latency; we include 40 hours of warm-up time for Option B.

Next steps: please confirm which option you want us to price with exact term lengths (6/12/24 months). If you want, we can sketch a hybrid: start A for 4–6 weeks then transition to B with pro-rated commit. I've attached the detailed offer (redwood-dedicated-offer-v1.pdf) and the assumptions sheet.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Dedicated Capacity
Redwood Inference

---
Attachments: redwood-dedicated-offer-v1.pdf (proposal), compute-assumptions.txt (notes)

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 09 Sep 2026 10:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Dedicated cluster sizing — internal pricing/discount check

Looping in finance and pricing cadence. Jonas — solid options. A few comments before we send a formal quote to Cory: 

- Can we tighten the starter min-gpu to 12 in exchange for a slightly longer ramp (12 -> 20 by week 6)? That helps procurement justify a smaller initial commitment.
- For Option B, propose a 10% net-first-year discount if they commit 12 months upfront and add a 3-month step-up protection (guarantees no price increase for first 3 months of ramp).
- Add a canary SLA clause (if canary fails, rollback with no penalty and 2-week extension of warm-up credits).

Ben — can you run margin on the 10% and confirm we can keep the warm-up credit hours as-is? Also flag any capacity constraints for Nov go-live (we'll need GPU lane guarantees).

Marissa
Director, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

Team — thanks, this is exactly the level of detail we needed. After internal review we've landed on a modified Balanced Growth: start with Option B but accept Marissa's suggested concessions. To be explicit:

- Contract start: Oct 15, 2026 (procurement needs PO lead time)
- Initial reserved min-gpus: 12 for first 6 weeks, then step to 48 once we pass the M1 onboarding milestone
- Committed term: 12 months with 10% upfront discount per Marissa's note
- Canary: 10% traffic for 14 days; if performance issues arise we'll trigger rollback & extension as discussed

Please prepare a formal SOW/quote and a draft PO template. Procurement will attach their standard terms but flagged a couple of security questions — I'll forward those in a separate thread.

Appreciate the speed here.

Cory Blake

Trident Therapeutics
